listener.note: revision 1 is the brief's exact YAML, used for the first (FAILED) fire below. revision 2 (stored verbatim, from Kestra's own PUT response) replaces `inputs.src` with a literal string so the chain could reach SUCCESS and produce hop-1/hop-2/hop-100 measurements; see findings.

revision_2.source:
id: listener
namespace: w13
triggers:
  - id: on_done
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.trigger.Flow
    states: [SUCCESS]
    inputs:
      src: "producer-fired"
inputs:
  - id: src
    type: STRING
tasks:
  - id: a
    type: io.kestra.plugin.core.log.Log
    message: "{{ inputs.src }}"
revision_2._provenance: verbatim body of Kestra's 200 response to `PUT /api/v1/main/flows/w13/listener` with the revision-2 YAML

listener2.note: unrestricted Flow trigger (no namespace/flowId condition), same shape as `listener`. Because neither trigger restricts its source, it fires on ANY execution's SUCCESS in the workspace, not only `listener`'s -- this is what produced the two-hop chain (and also an unbounded ping-pong between listener and listener2 that had to be stopped by deleting both flows; see findings).

listener_run1_FAILED_bad_inputs.log_at_failure: WARN Failed to trigger flow w13.listener for trigger on_done, invalid inputs; DEBUG io.kestra.core.exceptions.IllegalVariableEvaluationException: Unable to find `trigger` used in the expression `{{ trigger.executionId }}` at line 1, at io.kestra.plugin.core.trigger.Flow.evaluate(Flow.java:353)

ping_pong_measurement.note: Because both `listener` and `listener2` declare unrestricted Flow triggers (no namespace/flowId filter, matching the brief's own YAML for `listener`), the second producer run's chain did not stop at two hops: listener and listener2 kept re-firing each other's SUCCESS. 204 total executions were created in namespace w13 before both flows were deleted to stop it.
ping_pong_measurement.raw_query: All 204 execution ids were listed with `GET /api/v1/main/executions/search?namespace=w13&size=250`, then each was fetched in full with `GET /api/v1/main/executions/{id}` (204 requests, saved to local files) and grouped by `metadata.executionDepth` with a local script. That per-depth grouping (the count-by-depth table itself) was not retained; the two depth=100 records it surfaced were pulled back out of the 204 saved files and are stored verbatim above as `listener2_hop100_SUCCESS` / `listener_hop100_SUCCESS` (ids `5UAs4bqROsAznmWqGY6p2v`, `rKnfOVWKrUTO9rYL8QBZl`).
ping_pong_measurement.how_verified: Of the 204 raw execution records retained under this measurement, none carries `trigger.variables.executionId` equal to either depth-100 execution's own id -- i.e. no execution in the retained set was fired off `5UAs4bqROsAznmWqGY6p2v` or `rKnfOVWKrUTO9rYL8QBZl`, and no retained execution carries `metadata.executionDepth` above 100. This is checked directly against the 204 retained records, not asserted from an unretained aggregate.
ping_pong_measurement.refused_next_execution: Not captured. Kestra does not appear to materialize an execution record for a fire refused at the depth cap -- there is no execution object to fetch, only the absence of one. No log capture of a depth-limit refusal message was taken either (the logs API had already been shown to return results only for the render-failure case; see `listener_run1_FAILED_bad_inputs.log_at_failure`). So the depth-101 refusal is inferred from the absence of any depth>100 record among the 204 retained, not observed directly.

findings: Full key set of `execution.trigger.variables` for a Flow-fired execution: exactly `state`, `flowId`, `endDate`, `namespace`, `startDate`, `lastTaskId`, `executionId`, `flowRevision`, `executionLabels`. Verified identical (same 9-key sorted tuple) across all 204 measured executions that carried a `trigger` object, including the FAILED first attempt, the hop-1 SUCCESS (`QBI82sdiPStezk1byj0Yu`), and the hop-2 SUCCESS (`7e2wsms80NZ9Zh2b3DWtfI`). No `id`/`type` duplication inside `variables` beyond what is already at `trigger.id`/`trigger.type` (those two live one level up, not inside `variables`).

`state` IS the bare enum name: quoted verbatim from `listener_hop1_SUCCESS.trigger.variables.state` = `"SUCCESS"` (and identically `"SUCCESS"` in the FAILED run and the hop-2 run -- no execution reached a non-SUCCESS terminal state in this measurement, but the field is unquestionably the raw enum, not a wrapped/qualified form like `io.kestra...SUCCESS` or an object). This directly supports spec §4.1's unique index keying on `execution_trigger->'variables'->>'state'` as written -- no typed-column fallback (the W12 `scheduled_date` pattern) is needed.

Execution depth lives at `metadata.executionDepth` (an integer, not a `system.*` label and not inside `trigger`). It is ABSENT (not present, not null) on executions with no trigger (both `producer` runs have no `metadata.executionDepth` key at all). Hop 1 (`listener_hop1_SUCCESS`, fired directly by `producer`): `metadata.executionDepth = 1`. Hop 2 (`listener2_hop2_SUCCESS`, fired by `listener`'s SUCCESS): `metadata.executionDepth = 2`. The runaway ping-pong chain also produced two executions with `metadata.executionDepth = 100`, stored verbatim as `listener2_hop100_SUCCESS` (id `5UAs4bqROsAznmWqGY6p2v`) and `listener_hop100_SUCCESS` (id `rKnfOVWKrUTO9rYL8QBZl`) -- both quoted directly, not summarized. Within the 204 retained execution records, no execution's `trigger.variables.executionId` points at either of those two ids, and no retained record carries `executionDepth` above 100 (see `ping_pong_measurement.how_verified`); the depth-101 refusal itself was not captured (no execution object exists for a refused fire, and no refusal log line was retained -- see `ping_pong_measurement.refused_next_execution`). So `100` is the highest depth **checkable from this file**, and it corroborates the design's `DEFAULT_MAX_EXECUTION_DEPTH = 100` source constant, but the file cannot by itself prove 100 is the hard ceiling rather than merely the highest depth this particular 204-execution run happened to reach before cleanup stopped it.

`parentId` is ABSENT (not present as a key, let alone null) on every one of the 204 measured executions, flow-fired or not -- consistent with W6's 210/210 measurement and the spec's ratchet note. A flow-fired execution carries only the `trigger`/`trigger_execution_id` link, never `parentId`.

`inputs` did NOT render `{{ trigger.executionId }}`, as literally written in the brief's YAML for `listener`/`listener2`. Firing `listener` (revision 1, exact brief YAML) against `producer`'s first run produced a FAILED execution with NO `inputs` field at all (key entirely absent, not an empty object) and a queue-level WARN/DEBUG log pair: `Failed to trigger flow w13.listener for trigger on_done, invalid inputs` followed by `io.kestra.core.exceptions.IllegalVariableEvaluationException: Unable to find \`trigger\` used in the expression \`{{ trigger.executionId }}\` at line 1`, thrown from `io.kestra.plugin.core.trigger.Flow.evaluate(Flow.java:353)`. The render context used to evaluate a Flow trigger's own `inputs`/`when` has NO `trigger` binding in this pinned artifact -- it is not merely that `trigger.executionId` resolves to something unexpected, `trigger` itself is unbound at that point. This directly corroborates spec §4.5's stated non-goal ("Not done, and named: ... publishing `trigger.*` into the render context"): the egret port's decision not to publish `trigger.*` into the render context matches real Kestra's own behavior on this build, it is not a divergence. After revision 2 replaced `inputs.src` with a literal string (`"producer-fired"` / `"listener-fired"`), both listener flows reached SUCCESS and `inputs` appeared verbatim, e.g. `listener_hop1_SUCCESS.inputs = {"src": "producer-fired"}`.

The corpus's own real-world example (`corpus/valids/trigger-flow-listener.yaml`) never references `trigger.*` in its trigger `inputs`; it uses `outputs.only.value` instead -- independent evidence, from a file the brief did not point at, that `trigger.*` is not the corpus's own convention for wiring inputs on a Flow trigger.

`system.correlationId` on a chained fire is inherited from the ROOT of the chain, not the immediate trigger source: `listener2_hop2_SUCCESS.labels` carries `system.correlationId = 2sVbe2jtsuRuHS30oICal2` (the original `producer` run), even though its immediate trigger source is `listener`'s execution `QBI82sdiPStezk1byj0Yu`. Not asked for by the brief, but relevant since spec §4.5 explicitly defers `system.correlationId` (egret has no labels column) -- recorded here in case a future task revisits labels.
